title: perf(service-messaging): an idle dispatcher tick reads the database twice, not 18 and 10 times
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01LjZwNRFiG2fkp8SNf6rHNx?thread=cmsg_01LjZwNRFiG2fkp8SNf6rHNxECLC1evcjsCNG7ex4pEc8Z)_
Fixes #28383

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:通知调度器和 HTTP 调度器在 outbox 空闲时,每次轮询只读两次库(回收过期 claim 前先读一条、再用一条跨所有分区的"有没有到期行"读决定要不要逐分区探测),不再是 18 条和 10 条。
- 为什么改:cloud 实测一个空闲租户内核每分钟读库 56 次,全部是空转;这些读计入 Turso 的行读配额。
- 风险与回滚:有活时仍走原来的逐分区 claim/digest 路径,只多一次读;回收 UPDATE 的谓词不变,只在读到过期行时才执行。outbox 接口新增的 `hasDueWork` 是可选方法,自定义 outbox 不实现就保持旧行为。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-messaging/src/dispatcher.ts`(`runTick` 里的门)、`src/sql-outbox.ts`(`reapExpired` 与 `hasDueWork`)、`src/dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts`(语句数钉子)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts src/http-dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts`,预期 13 个用例全绿,空闲 tick 钉在 2 条 SQL。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

An idle tick of each delivery dispatcher now costs **two SQL statements**, whatever `partitionCount` is. Measured at the client (knex `query` events) on a harness with one global `afterUpdate` hook, the kernel shape cloud measured:

| Dispatcher | main `ac09e7b85` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `NotificationDispatcher` | 18 | **2** |
| `HttpDispatcher` | 10 | **2** |

The card's bar is ≤ 6 per dispatcher.

- **Candidate 1: the reap writes only when there is something to reap.** `reapExpired` in `sql-outbox.ts` and `sql-http-outbox.ts` first reads one expired `in_flight` id (`fields: ['id'], limit: 1`). If it finds none, it returns. If it finds one, it runs the predicate `UPDATE`, which is unchanged, so every claim expired by then still goes back to `pending`, not only the one the read saw. On a kernel the old unconditional `UPDATE` was two statements (the engine reads the matched rows for the per-row `afterUpdate` dispatch, then writes); it is now one read.
- **Candidates 2 and 3: one due-work read gates every partition probe, digest probes included.** `INotificationOutbox` and `IHttpOutbox` gain an optional `hasDueWork({ now })`. It asks, in one `SELECT id … LIMIT 1` across every partition and organization, whether any `pending` row is due. The predicate is the claim's own with the partition term dropped, and for notifications with the `digest_key` arm dropped, so it covers immediate and batched rows alike. `runTick` asks it after the reap. If nothing is due, the tick ends there: no partition lock is taken and no claim or digest probe runs. If something is due, the tick runs the full per-partition pass exactly as before, for one extra read. Both built-in stores (SQL and memory) implement it. A store without it keeps probing every partition. `DueWorkOptions` and `HttpDueWorkOptions` are exported.
- `partitionCount` and the stored `partition_key` are unchanged.

## Why

An idle hosted tenant kernel read its database 56 times a minute with nothing queued: 2 ticks × (18 + 10) at the framework's 30 s idle ceiling, plus a 140-statement backoff ramp in the first minute. Those reads count against Turso's rows-read quota, and cloud#2177 once had a staging account suspended for reads. With this PR an idle minute costs 8 statements at the 30 s ceiling.

## Tests

- `dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts` and `http-dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts` now count SQL statements on the delivery table at the client as well as engine calls, with a global no-op `afterUpdate` hook registered so a predicate `UPDATE` is the read-then-write pair it is on a kernel. On this harness, main measures 18 and 10 statements per tick, the same figures cloud measured.
  - The idle pin: `{ update: 0, find: 2 × TICKS }` engine calls, and exactly `2 × TICKS` SQL statements, all `SELECT`. This replaces the old `≤ TICKS × (1 + 2 × partitionCount)` and `≤ TICKS × (1 + partitionCount)` ceilings.
  - New: a row deferred into the future (notification `notBefore`; an HTTP retry acked with `nextRetryAt`) keeps the tick at two reads and goes out on the first tick after it comes due.
  - New (notification): a due digest-only outbox is found by the due-work read and collapsed on that tick.
  - The crash-recovery legs now also assert the reap's `UPDATE` ran exactly once when a claim had expired. This guards against a reap that never writes.
  - The legacy-outbox legs (no `reap`, and so no `hasDueWork`) are unchanged and still see `2 × partitionCount` and `partitionCount` claims a tick.
- Pins that assumed the old shape, reconciled:
  - `sql-outbox-audit-columns.test.ts`: its fake engine's scripted `find` queue now opens with a reap read that finds a stale row, so the reap `UPDATE` payload it checks for `updated_at` is still produced.
  - `system-context.pin.test.ts`: the population counts include the reap reads and one `hasDueWork` call, so the new reads are also held to the explicit system opt-in.
  - `http-dispatcher-idle-backoff.test.ts`: it timestamped a tick at `claim()`, which an idle tick no longer calls. It now timestamps at `reap()`, which every tick calls once first, as the notification side's file already did.

## Acceptance notes

- **Deviation from the dispatch's mechanism assumption (candidate 2).** The dispatch described "one probe across the partitions this process holds". The due-work read here spans all partitions and takes no lock, and it gates the per-partition pass instead of replacing it. Lock state is unknown until each `acquire`, and on the common single-node or memory lock every partition is held anyway. A read that moves nothing needs no lock, as with the reap. Keeping the per-partition claims under their locks leaves the busy path, the batch size per partition and the digest-under-lock rule exactly as they were. On a multi-node cluster, a node whose partitions are all held elsewhere pays the same lock attempts as before whenever something is due anywhere, and two reads when nothing is.
- **Candidate 3 is folded into the one read**, which is the card's first option ("fold into the claim probe"). A busy tick still runs both probes in every held partition. Narrowing the busy path is not what this card measured.
- **Out of scope, as dispatched:**
  - Candidate 4: wake at the next due time instead of a blind ceiling (`packages/core/src/dispatch-loop.ts`).
  - Candidate 5: a persisted watermark for the objectql lifecycle sweep's first run 60 s after every boot.
  - The backoff ramp's first-minute price now falls with the per-tick price (5 ramp ticks × 4 statements instead of × 28). cloud re-measures under cloud#3413.
- The new reads add `ORDER BY id` (the engine's default when a `limit` is set) over a `limit 1`. That is one row from the primary key ordering, not a scan cost this card measured.

## Verification

All readings at head `95f4da30a` unless stated.

<details><summary>Statement counts (before / after)</summary>

A throwaway measurement on main `ac09e7b85` (not committed), with and without a global `afterUpdate` hook, one tick each over an empty outbox:

- no hook: notification 17, HTTP 9; with the hook: notification 18, HTTP 10. The hook shape is `select * … where status = ? and claimed_at < ?` then the `update`, followed by one or two `select id … partition_key = ?` per partition.
- After the change, both shapes: notification 2, HTTP 2. Each is `select id … where status = ? and claimed_at < ? … limit ?`, then `select id … where status = ? and ((next_… is null) or (next_… <= ?)) … limit ?`.

</details>

<details><summary>Package tests and typecheck</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging test`: Test Files 62 passed (62), Tests 759 passed (759). Lock VERDICT command-exit 0 at `18e1c546b`. The later commit only adds the changeset and one `as HttpClaimCredential` cast in a test.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging typecheck`: exit 0 at `95f4da30a`. At `18e1c546b` the first run caught one TS2345 in the new HTTP retry leg (an `HttpDelivery` passed as the claim credential), fixed with the cast the dispatcher itself uses.
- The two idle-cost files at `95f4da30a`: 13 passed (13).

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored, git diff HEAD empty, marker grep 0)</summary>

Tests import `src/` relatively, so no dist rebuild sits between mutation and run.

- A: the `hasDueWork` gate in `NotificationDispatcher.runTick` replaced by a marker. Notification idle-cost file: 2 failed / 5 passed (the idle pin: `find: 170` vs `20`, 17 statements vs 2; the deferred-row pin).
- B: `SqlHttpOutbox.reapExpired`'s early return replaced by a marker. HTTP idle-cost file: 2 failed / 4 passed (the idle pin: `update: 10` vs `0`; the retry pin: 4 statements vs 2).

</details>

<details><summary>Dispatch gates and lint</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 62 families derived from 15 paths vs merge base `ac09e7b85` (473 changed lines, under the 3000 threshold). Every command was run with stdin closed, and each exit code was captured to disk before any pipe.
- `--ran` reconciliation: 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN; it exits 0.
- Every derived command exited 0. Three first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) and were re-run after their prerequisite:
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n` after a full `pnpm build` (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
  - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` after `git fetch --unshallow origin main` (48 cases pass).
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`): lock VERDICT command-exit 0.

</details>

- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (See Verification.)

- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
